notes:
Account snapshot — Lyra builds a cloud-first conversational layer for mid-market contact centers. Primary goals: (1) reduce avg handle time with agent-assist and accurate tool-calls into Zendesk/Ticketing; (2) automatic ticket summarization with citation links back to canonical KB; (3) reliable service during marketing spikes (Black Friday equivalent) and monthly billing cycles.

Key quotes / call snippets: "We cannot tolerate hallucinations — citations must map to doc IDs and timestamps." — VP Product. "If we can trust the system to call the right support tool actions, we can reduce Tier 1 FTE by ~22%." — Head of Ops.

Data sources: Zendesk historic tickets (~3M rows), Confluence KB, internal S3 PDFs (policy docs), product changelogs from Git, and periodic vendor-supplied knowledge bundles. Need multi-source retrieval with per-source freshness and a citation ranking mechanism. Prefer vector store compatibility (Weaviate, Pinecone) but willing to try Redwood's managed embeddings if latency/COST look good.

Security: SAML SSO + SCIM for provisioning, org-level audit logs, KMS integration for key separation, able to demonstrate EU/US residency split. SOC2 required, ISO27001 preferred. Legal flagged retention controls and delete workflows.

POC scope (agreed in scoping call): ingest sample KB (1M doc chunks), build retrieval pipeline, RAG for ticket summarization (batch), agent-assist streaming RAG for live agent UI (low-latency citations), and tool-calling flow to create/update Zendesk tickets. Success criteria: 95th %ile latency <250ms for agent assist lookups, citation precision >85% on labeled test prompts, stable throughput 200 req/s under synthetic spike with graceful fallback to cached summaries.

Commercials: targeting Dedicated or Private; mid-range ARR expected. Asked for canary rollout plan and cost/latency tradeoff models (batching, quantization).

Risks/concerns: security timeline may push procurement past forecast; data mapping (ticket -> KB link) requires custom enrichers; ownership of vector DB vs Redwood-managed embeddings still undecided.

Stubs/refs: drive links above, Fireflies recordings for 2/20 security and 3/2 scoping, Jira tickets INF-1092 (ingest errors) and SEC-7234 (crypto/KMS questions).
use_case_summary: Lyra wants a phased rollout: 1) ticket summarization (high quality citations, nightly batch retriever), 2) agent-assist with streaming RAG + live citations and linkbacks, 3) tool-calling integration to Zendesk for triage actions. Long-term: cross-region residency, quantized models for cost, and automatic fallback policies under spike conditions.
requirements: Multi-source RAG: consolidate Zendesk, Confluence, S3 PDFs; per-source freshness metadata
Citation linking: return doc ID + stable URL + excerpt + provenance score
Latency: 95th percentile <250ms for agent lookup; tail latency protection and prefetching
Throughput & reliability: sustain 200 req/s sustained with 3x burst capability; autoscaling + graceful degradation
Security: SSO (SAML/SCIM), KMS integration, SOC2 compliance report, audit logs retention controls
Tool-calling: reliable, idempotent action calls into Zendesk with retry semantics and verifiable human override
Eval metrics: citation precision/recall, accuracy for summarization, hallucination rate thresholds, freshness staleness window
